scenarioStory.history: Patient was standing outside a convenience store when he was shot once in the left anterior chest during an apparent robbery attempt. Bystanders called 911 immediately; police secured the scene prior to EMS entry. Patient was initially able to speak but is now increasingly short of breath and anxious.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 26-year-old male sitting upright with a single gunshot wound to the left anterior chest. He is increasingly dyspneic with visible jugular venous distention and tracheal deviation. → Tension pneumothorax decompressed: Crew recognizes the classic signs of tension pneumothorax and performs needle decompression of the left chest, with immediate improvement in breath sounds and hemodynamics. → Rapid transport initiated: With the tension physiology resolved, the patient is packaged and transported rapidly to a trauma center with continued reassessment en route.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Gunshot wound to the left chest

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 26-year-old male sitting upright with a single gunshot wound to the left anterior chest. He is increasingly dyspneic with visible jugular venous distention and tracheal deviation.

scenarioEvents.name: Tension pneumothorax decompressed
scenarioEvents.description: Crew recognizes the classic signs of tension pneumothorax and performs needle decompression of the left chest, with immediate improvement in breath sounds and hemodynamics.
relatedChecklist: Perform MARCH primary survey; identify absent left breath sounds, JVD, and hypotension
Needle decompression of left 2nd intercostal space, midclavicular line
Apply semi-occlusive dressing over the open chest wound
Establish large-bore IV access; give 500 mL crystalloid bolus for SBP <90 mmHg
Apply supplemental oxygen to maintain SpO2 greater than 94%

scenarioEvents.name: Rapid transport initiated
scenarioEvents.description: With the tension physiology resolved, the patient is packaged and transported rapidly to a trauma center with continued reassessment en route.
relatedChecklist: Reassess breath sounds, vitals, and mental status serially en route
Transport to trauma center; minimize scene time (goal under 10 minutes) for penetrating torso trauma

scenarioEvents.name: Decompression delayed
scenarioEvents.description: The crew prioritizes IV access and fluids without recognizing the tension physiology. Intrathoracic pressure continues to rise, and the patient rapidly deteriorates toward obstructive shock.
relatedChecklist: Recognize worsening tension physiology; perform immediate needle decompression
